messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: P1: sudden spike in 502/504s from API Gateway (edge) — 5xx rate 22% over 3m, tail latencies increasing. Auto-pager fired. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/edge/edge-errors?view=recent

PagerDuty: Paging Sam R (on-call)

Sam R: ack. I'm looking. Is this global or single region?

Lina M: seeing errors almost exclusively originating from apigw-us-east-1 -> upstream svc-payments. Error snippet in logs: `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` then `connection reset by peer` on upstream socket.

Ethan V: no recent deploys in svc-payments or edge in last 6h. However DNS autoscaler jobs ran ~40m ago to increase svc-payments endpoints in us-east. Could be ephemeral.

DevOps Bot: Edge pool metrics: CPU/mem normal. Socket queue depth on edge-proxy-07 trending towards limit. `netstat` on node shows many TIME_WAIT and a growing count of `syn_recv`.

Sam R: interesting. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on svc-payments side or a load balancer backend flapping. Lina, can you curl the upstream directly from edge-proxy pod? Also paste the edge-proxy config (snippet) for upstream timeouts.

Lina M: from edge-proxy-07:
```
curl -sv -H 'Host: svc-payments' https://10.23.45.67:443/health
* Connected to 10.23.45.67 (10.23.45.67) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: svc-payments
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
< x-edge: edge-proxy-07
< 
504: upstream timed out
```

Lina M: edge config excerpt:
```
upstream svc-payments {
  keepalive 1024;
  proxy_connect_timeout 5s;
  proxy_read_timeout 15s;
}
```

Sam R: keepalive high on edge. If upstream instances are short-lived (DNS autoscaler) they may be rejecting connections. Let's check svc-payments pod logs for accept errors and ephemeral port exhaustion. Lina, Ethan, run `ss -s` on a payments node and post summary.

Ethan V: svc-payments node ss summary:
```
TCP:   15000 total, 6500 established, 700 syn_recv, 3600 time_wait
```

Ethan V: also seeing kernel log messages: `nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet` around the spike. That suggests conntrack exhaustion on the kube-proxy host.

Sam R: aha. conntrack/full would cause dropped packets and upstream resets leading to 502/504. Quick mitigations: 1) bump conntrack max via sysctl on affected nodes 2) add temporary iptables rule to reduce conntrack timeout for ESTABLISHED? (risky) 3) shift some traffic to eu-central to reduce pressure while we patch.

Lina M: bumping sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max from 262144 -> 524288 on two affected nodes now. Command: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=524288`

DevOps Bot: Noted: sysctl change applied to nodes node-12 and node-14. Monitoring conntrack table usage.

Sam R: good. Also let's scale svc-payments replicas up by 3 to give more endpoints and reduce per-pod conn counts: `kubectl scale deploy/svc-payments --replicas=10 -n platform`

Ethan V: scaling now. New pods starting.

Customer Success: CS reports customers X and Y seeing elevated failures for web checkouts. I'm posting a short customer-facing status: "We're investigating intermittent payment failures affecting some regions. Mitigations in progress."

Lina M: after conntrack bump + extra pods, 5xx rate dropped to 8% within 6 minutes. Some residual 502s but tail latency improving.

Sam R: staying cautious. We'll also remove the DNS autoscaler job that churned endpoints while we assess. Ethan, keep conntrack bump until end of incident; we'll add a permanent config via daemonset patch after RCA.

Ethan V: removed autoscaler job and pinned endpoints count. Creating k8s patch to set sysctl via privileged daemonset for all nodes. PR to infra: https://git.redwood.example/pr/2791

DevOps Bot: Incident Bot updated: 5xx now 6.5% (5m), connections metrics normalizing.

Sam R: great. Plan for next hour: 1) keep traffic in us-east but monitor 2) leave conntrack increased and scale adjustments in place 3) infra to deploy daemonset to make conntrack change persistent 4) CS to prepare customer message with affected window and impacted regions.

Customer Success: drafting customer note now; will share for review in 10m.

Lina M: logs show a handful of payment pods still returning RSTs during startup — those correlate with the autoscaler churn window. Post-incident action: tighten autoscaler cooldown to avoid endpoint churn.

Sam R: handing off monitoring to Ethan V at 18:30 UTC. If 5xx climbs above 10%, re-page.

Ethan V: taking handoff. I'll follow up with a succinct RCA and remediation tickets.

Sam R: thanks team. Incident mitigated for now. Postmortem owner: Lina M. Incident Bot: mark as mitigated and generate timeline.

Incident Bot: Incident status -> mitigated. Archive will be created.
